title: County neonicotinoid use did not lower grassland or insectivorous bird counts on US Breeding Bird Survey routes in 2008-2014 or 1995-2007; the published effect is about 6 times the data limit
abstract: Question: Li, Miao and Khanna (2020) reported that +100 kg of county neonicotinoid use decreased US grassland birds by 2.2% and insectivorous birds by 1.6% in 2008-2014 (cumulative 9.7%). Is this effect present in the same public data? Data: North American Breeding Bird Survey 2026 release (standard runs, contiguous US) and USGS EPest county estimates 1992-2014. Method (plan written before outcomes): route-by-observer and year fixed effects, state-clustered errors; region-by-year effects; lead placebo; event study 1994-2014 with the 1999-2001 to 2012-2014 county increase; an independent period 1995-2007; a control guild; injection of the published effect into observed counts. Results: in 2008-2014 (3,024 routes, 14,767 runs), grassland counts changed by -0.06% per 100 kg (95% CI -0.16 to +0.04) and insectivores by -0.05% (-0.12 to +0.01); control birds -0.02%. Fifteen model variants (county aggregation, lags, cumulative use, state trends, EPest-low, other pesticides, 20-km disc intensity) gave grassland values from -0.09% to +0.06%. Injected effects of -2.2%, -1.1% and -0.5% were recovered as -0.96%, -0.61% and -0.36%; the observed interval excludes all three, so true effects larger than about -0.25% to -0.37% are not compatible with the data. The event study showed no cumulative loss (2012-2014: +0.03%, -0.15 to +0.20). 1995-2007 gave +0.02% (grassland) and -0.02% (insectivores). Some insectivore estimates were -0.04% to -0.15% with intervals below zero, but control birds gave similar values. Limitations: comparison values come from the authors' press releases; EPest is modelled county use; the start-point county and log(1+count) attenuate effects (quantified by injection); 2015+ EPest omits seed treatments and was not used.
